prompt_text: 안녕하세요. 저는 제 목소리로 음성 샘플을 만들고 있습니다. 오늘 날씨는 맑고 바람이 조금 불었습니다. 열두 시 삼십 분에 회의를 시작하겠습니다.

samples.text: Most projects in this hackathon show you what an agent accomplishes. Backstop takes the opposite side. It shows you the deploy that got blocked.

Two things went wrong in our own system while we were building it. The same email went out twice. And a workflow step vanished, while the agent reported that it was complete. Both times, the unit tests were green.
No human could have caught either one. There is nowhere to ask whether a purchase order went out twice, and when a workflow says done, nothing contradicts it.

So Backstop records every tool call your agent makes into an append-only ledger. Before a new version ships, it rewinds six weeks of that ledger against the new code, and computes which side effects this version would run again.
On our seed ledger, the answer is three duplicate purchase orders. The gate returns exit code one, and the deploy is blocked. One duplicate is enough.
The model decides nothing here. The verdict is set arithmetic, a pure function, with unit tests attached. Take the language model out entirely, and deploy blocked is still deploy blocked.
